source.title: Enumerating number fields
source.versionRead: Published Annals PDF, all 11 pages (487–497), including Sections 1–4 and references; downloaded and read completely. No claim to have compared the arXiv versions.
readSections: Section 1, pp. 487–489: Theorems 1–2, field-component convention, historical bounds and strategy
Section 2, pp. 489–490: canonical metric/measure, successive minima, product-span argument and Proposition 1
Section 3, pp. 491–495: first jets, integer parameters, relation lattice, dual Gram determinant, truncation and Proposition 2
Section 4, pp. 495–496: central-binomial choice, coefficient enumeration and isolated-point Bezout

summary: Complete extraction/routing of the published paper, continuing the merged partial checkpoint while preserving all 42 original item IDs. The 49 items distinguish 10 pinned-library inputs, 2 existing planned interfaces and 37 missing consumer/generic statements routed exactly once. The source proves independent delta^2-short integers, explicit small Jacobian-open component models, logarithmic equation/variable bounds and N_n(H)<=n^(Q*n*log(n)^3)*H^(Q*log(n)^3). Existing root discriminants, degree-bounded polynomials, product-measure covolumes, lattice indices, Schwartz–Zippel and abstract etale classification are imports. The four routes are two source additions, generic double-point interpolation, and a Part II of EffectiveBounds. Complete denotes extraction and ownership, not a closed blueprint, an accepted route, or a Lean implementation.

items.name: Signed discriminant and root-discriminant notation
items.statement: For a number field K of degree n, use d_K = NumberField.discr K in Z and write delta = |d_K|^(1/n). Here n is positive. The root is a real power of the absolute value, not of the signed discriminant.
items.note: Discriminant/Defs.lean supplies the signed invariant, nonvanishing and Q-algebra-isomorphism invariance. Discriminant/Basic.lean, lines 74–86, actually defines NumberField.rootDiscr with exactly |discr K|^(finrank Q K)^(-1); this corrects the inherited checkpoint's negative claim. Positivity follows from nonzero integer discriminant. Use |d_K| in imaginary examples.

items.name: Archimedean supremum gauge
items.statement: Use the supremum over all embeddings tau:K -> C, equivalently the maximum over the real places and one representative of each complex conjugate pair. For x in K, its canonical embedding has norm at most R exactly when every |tau(x)| is at most R.
items.note: Pinned CanonicalEmbedding/Basic.lean read. Keep this sup gauge distinct from the canonical Euclidean metric and from the coefficient Euclidean norm. Tests: Q, a real quadratic field, and an imaginary quadratic field.

items.name: Ring of integers in Minkowski space
items.statement: The mixed embedding of O_K is a full Z-lattice in the real vector space with one real coordinate per real place and one complex coordinate per complex place; its real dimension is n. An integral basis gives its real lattice basis.
items.note: Pinned CanonicalEmbedding/Basic.lean read, including the anonymous IsZLattice instance following span_latticeBasis. Consume the existing carrier rather than defining a competing lattice.

items.name: Multiplicative norm versus field norm
items.statement: For x in K, the product over infinite places of the absolute value of x, with multiplicity one at real places and two at complex places, is |Norm_(K/Q)(x)|.
items.locator: Section 2, p. 489, input to the nonzero-integer lower bound
items.note: Pinned CanonicalEmbedding/Basic.lean read; multiplicity two is essential.

items.name: Canonical measure comparison for the short-integer argument
items.statement: If K has signature (r1,s), n=r1+2s, put <x,y> = sum_real x_i y_i + sum_complex (x_j conjugate(y_j)+conjugate(x_j)y_j). Its Euclidean Haar measure mu_can equals 2^s times standard product Lebesgue measure. The sup unit ball has mu_can-volume 2^r1(2*pi)^s >= 2^n.
items.note: Only the weighted-metric/product-measure bridge is new. Mathlib's mixed-space volume and even its euclidean.volumePreserving_toMixed use unweighted complex Euclidean coordinates. Multiplying the measure by 2^s gives Couveignes's convention. Prove the identity by scaling each complex real coordinate by sqrt(2); the determinant is 2^s. Test s=0 and Q(i); never rescale a norm by silently replacing the measure.

items.name: Canonical covolume of O_K
items.statement: For an actual Z-basis beta of O_K and its embedding matrix A=(tau_j(beta_i)), the canonical Gram matrix is A conjugate(A)^t. Thus covol_mu_can(O_K)=|det A|=sqrt(|d_K|)=delta^(n/2).
items.note: The product-measure theorem is baseline-mixed-covolume below, not new work. This item is its canonical-measure specialization using measure-normalization and the same fundamental domain: multiply 2^(-s)*sqrt|d_K| by 2^s. An actual integral basis, not the short independent family, identifies |det A|. The final real-power identity uses n>0 and |d_K|>=1.

items.name: A nonzero algebraic integer has sup gauge at least one
items.statement: For x in O_K, x != 0 implies max_tau |tau(x)| >= 1: its field norm is a nonzero rational integer, whereas all conjugates of modulus less than one would give norm of modulus less than one.
items.note: Consumer consequence of norm-product, integrality of the algebra norm and Int.one_le_abs; searches in both canonical-embedding and discriminant APIs did not locate the exact sup-gauge bound. A hypothetical gauge<1 makes every factor in the nonzero norm product <1. Do not assert every individual conjugate has modulus >=1 (units give counterexamples).

items.name: Minkowski second theorem: upper product bound with witnesses
items.statement: For a full lattice Lambda in a real vector space of positive finite dimension m and a compact convex symmetric body B with nonempty interior, the successive minima satisfy product_i lambda_i(B,Lambda) * vol(B) <= 2^m*covol(Lambda). Supply independent lattice vectors attaining the successive-minimum bounds, so the same upper bound controls the product of their B-gauges.
items.locator: Section 2, p. 490 and Section 3, p. 494; Siegel [19], Lecture III, Section 4, Theorem 16
items.note: Merged reviewed audit explicitly says the second theorem/successive-minima product bound is absent in both pinned libraries; GN.1 already plans it. The first theorem alone is insufficient.

items.name: Ordered product bound
items.statement: If 1 <= a_1 <= ... <= a_m and product_i a_i <= V, then for 1 <= i <= m, a_i <= V^(1/(m+1-i)).
items.locator: Section 2, p. 490; repeated with m=ell in Section 3, p. 494
items.note: A small arithmetic consequence, not a new asymptotic theory. Prove a_i^(m+1-i)<=product a_j<=V using a_j>=1 for j<i and a_j>=a_i for j>=i, then the increasing positive-root function. Searches of ordered-product/rpow APIs did not locate this exact indexed package. Consumer-specific sorted-vector extraction remains in the Part II.

items.name: More than half a basis of small integral elements
items.statement: Minkowski second with mu_can gives Z-independent omega_1,...,omega_n in O_K with ordered gauges and product <= delta^(n/2). For m=floor(n/2)+1, the first m have gauge <= delta.
items.note: These independent elements are not claimed to be a basis of O_K. m>n/2, including even n, is the dimension argument needed next.

items.name: Products of a more-than-half-dimensional subspace span the field
items.statement: For a finite field extension K/k of dimension n and a k-subspace V with 2*dim_k(V)>n, the k-span of {ab | a,b in V} is K. In particular the products omega_i*omega_j for i,j<=m span K over Q.
items.note: For nonzero f:K->k, the form f(ab) is nondegenerate: choose c with f(c)!=0 and pair a!=0 with a^(-1)c. Its annihilator of V has dimension n-dim V; V contained in it contradicts 2 dim V>n. This elementary field-specific lemma was not found in either pinned tree; no Galois or separability assumption is needed. It remains a short lemma beside its arithmetic consumer, not a competing bilinear-form theory.

items.name: Proposition 1: independent short algebraic integers
items.statement: For every number field K of degree n and root discriminant delta there are n Z-linearly independent alpha_i in O_K such that |tau(alpha_i)| <= delta^2 for every i and every complex embedding tau.
items.note: Select independent products from product-span. No integral-basis or monogenicity assertion is made.

items.name: Bounded-degree coefficient space and homogenization interface
items.statement: For r>=1 and d>=0, let M be the monomials in r variables of total degree <=d, so #M=binom(d+r,d). The coefficient module V_R=R^M is identified with the degree-bounded polynomials; over C, homogenization at x_0 identifies it with degree-d homogeneous forms and H^0(P^r_C,O(d)). Give V_R the Euclidean metric making M orthonormal and V_Z=Z^M.
items.note: Import baseline-bounded-polynomials (the actual restrictTotalDegree submodule, restricted monomial basis and finite generation). New here are the joint finite-monomial count, fixed-degree homogenization/H^0 comparison and coefficient-isometry contract; do not construct polynomial rings or a second degree-bounded carrier. API: coefficient/evaluation/partial-derivative maps, homogenization/dehomogenization inverses, dimension binom(d+r,d), and orthonormal coordinate identification. Tests: r=1 gives d+1; d=0 gives constants; r=2,d=2 gives six monomials, not nine.

items.name: Double points and well-poised first jets
items.statement: For n pairwise distinct points P_tau in A^r_C subset P^r_C with ideal sheaf I, define 2P by I^2. It has length n(r+1). Call 2P well poised in degree d when H^0(P^r_C,O(d))->H^0(2P,O(d)) is surjective.
items.note: API: length, restriction map, independence of ordering, affine-coordinate description; tests one point and r=1. Do not confuse I^2 with a reduced union or with a second-order jet retaining quadratic terms.

items.name: First-jet matrix criterion
items.statement: In the monomial basis of degree <=d, the map in double-points is the n(r+1)-by-M matrix whose rows are values and each of the r first partial derivatives at the n points. Well-poisedness is equivalent to row rank n(r+1); a nonzero maximal minor defines an open full-rank locus.
items.note: The r+1 blocks are stacked vertically. API must expose the value projection and the derivative map on its kernel, not just a matrix-rank predicate.

items.name: Alexander-Hirschowitz in the exception-free degree range
items.statement: Over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, for r>=1, d>=5 and n>=1 with n(r+1)<=binom(d+r,d), there is a nonempty Zariski-open locus of ordered distinct n-tuples in (A^r)^n for which the first-jet evaluation map in degree <=d is surjective.
items.note: Brambilla–Ottaviani arXiv:math/0701409v2, Sections 1–6 (pp. 1–19), were read, including the proof of Theorem 6.4 and its low-degree dependencies. All exceptions in Theorem 1.1 have d<=4. Intersect the generic projective locus with the dense affine chart and distinct-point locus; it is not a theorem for every configuration. The owner must include residual/trace sequences, the curvilinear lemma, semicontinuity/degeneration and the cubic/quartic base certificates; no proof by merely calling d>=5 exception-free. No positive-characteristic extension is claimed.

items.name: Integer-grid nonvanishing
items.statement: Let F be a characteristic-zero field. A nonzero polynomial in N variables with degree in each variable at most D does not vanish on all of {0,...,D}^N subset F^N.
items.locator: Section 3, p. 492, passage from a nonzero minor to bounded u_ij
items.note: This exact per-variable statement follows by induction from the univariate root bound; no exact finite-box declaration was found in the inspected MvPolynomial APIs. The paper's application can avoid introducing it: its determinant has TOTAL degree <=d*n*(r+1), so baseline-total-degree-grid gives a nonzero integer point directly. Preserve this source statement, but implement only the needed existing-lemma specialization unless another consumer requires the stronger box theorem. Generic real coefficients cannot be rounded to obtain the result.

items.name: Integral parameters and evaluation maps
items.statement: For the independent short alpha_i and integers u_ij, set kappa_j=sum_i u_ij alpha_i. Define epsilon_Q:Q[x_1,...,x_r]->K by x_j |-> kappa_j and its real and complex base changes. In complex embedding coordinates P_tau=(sum_i u_ij tau(alpha_i))_j.
items.note: API: generator evaluation, base-change commuting squares, coordinate equality and integrality. Tests zero parameters, permutation of embeddings and a non-integral-basis family alpha.

items.name: Bounded integral parameters with surjective first jets
items.statement: For d>=5, r>=1 and n(r+1)<=M, some maximal minor of the first-jet matrix of parameterized-generators is a nonzero polynomial in the nr parameters, with degree in each u_ij at most d*n*(r+1). Hence parameters can be chosen with 0<=u_ij<=d*n*(r+1) so 2P is well poised.
items.note: The embedding matrix of the Q-basis alpha is invertible, so pulling back the generic rank locus leaves a nonzero maximal minor. Each value/derivative row has parameter total degree <=d (derivative rows <=d-1); the determinant has total degree <=d*n*(r+1), stronger than the displayed per-variable bound. Thus the existing Schwartz–Zippel theorem suffices. Distinctness and closed immersion follow from full first-jet rank; arbitrary parameters need not give distinct points.

items.name: Well-poised jets imply surjective value evaluation
items.statement: For the chosen parameters, degree-<=d value evaluation V_C->C^n is surjective. By scalar extension, V_Q->K and V_R->K_R are surjective. Consequently the corresponding maps Spec K, Spec K_R and Spec K_C into affine space are closed immersions.
items.note: Do not infer that V_Z->O_K is surjective. Descent uses faithful extension of scalars for vector spaces, not an arbitrary flatness assertion over Z.

items.name: Saturated integral relation lattice
items.statement: Let W=ker(epsilon_R restricted to V_R), and L=W intersect V_Z=ker(epsilon_Z,d). Then L is saturated in Z^M, rank_Z L=ell=M-n, and its real span is W. Let Lperp=Wperp intersect Z^M.
items.note: Interpret the printed L tensor_Q R as the real span, or L tensor_Z R; L itself is a Z-module. API: membership iff evaluation zero, saturatedness, rank and scalar-extension map; tests kappa=0 without invoking the full-rank hypothesis and a full-rank example.

items.name: Primitive orthogonal sublattices of a unimodular lattice
items.statement: For a rational subspace W of Euclidean R^M, the primitive lattices W intersect Z^M and Wperp intersect Z^M have equal covolumes in their respective real spans, using the induced Euclidean measures.
items.note: Couveignes explicitly invokes Martinet Corollary 1.3.5. GN.0's existing covolume and determinant APIs do not themselves assert this orthogonal-sublattice comparison. The completed IntegralLattices README/audit and Dual/Overlattice/OrthogonalSum searches give discriminant groups and orthogonal sums, not this Euclidean-measure conclusion. Proof route: extend a basis of the saturated sublattice to a Z-basis of Z^M; the complementary dual basis spans the orthogonal lattice; block Gram/Schur-complement determinants and unimodularity give equal squared covolumes. No new IntegralLattice carrier or gluing theorem is proposed. Check Z(1,1) and Z(1,-1), both covolume sqrt(2); a nonsaturated replacement invalidates equality.

items.name: Dual evaluation image and its finite index
items.statement: For Odual=Hom_Z(O_K,Z), the transpose of epsilon_Z,d maps Odual injectively into Lperp, and its image has full rank n. Hence covol(L)=covol(Lperp)<=covol(image(epsilon_Z,d^t)).
items.note: Full rational rank gives injectivity and a rank-n image in Lperp; integral surjectivity is not required. Use baseline-lattice-index after an orthonormal identification of Wperp with R^n to get the covolume inequality. API: transpose pairing, annihilation, rank and index. An even-valued full-rank row Z^M->Z gives a strict index and tests the direction.

items.name: Dual-image covolume and the evaluation Gram matrix
items.statement: Let M0=(m(P_tau)) be the n-by-M value matrix and let T be the inverse embedding matrix of an actual integral basis of O_K. Then T*M0 has integer entries and covol(image(epsilon_Z,d^t))^2=det(M0*conjugate(M0)^t)/|d_K|.
items.note: The basis defining T is an integral basis, not the merely independent short alpha_i. Use the Hermitian Gram matrix; complex transpose without conjugation is not the positive matrix needed for Hadamard.

items.name: Archimedean evaluation height
items.statement: For the chosen u, every |tau(kappa_j)|<=n^2*d*(r+1)*delta^2. Every degree-<=d monomial value has modulus <=[n^2*d*(r+1)]^d*delta^(2d). Put D=M*[n^2*d*(r+1)]^(2d)*delta^(4d); the diagonal entries of M0*conjugate(M0)^t are at most D.
items.note: Retain the number M of columns in the Gram bound. The passage from degrees <=d to degree d uses a base bound >=1.

items.name: Covolume bound for integral relations
items.statement: Hadamard applied to the positive Hermitian Gram matrix gives covol(L)<=D^(n/2)/sqrt(|d_K|)<=D^(n/2).
items.note: Use hadamard-gram (separately extracted generic input), gram-discriminant-identity and the dual-image inclusion. The final weakening uses |d_K|>=1. A file named Matrix/Hadamard contains the entrywise product, not this inequality; searches of determinant/Gram/inner-product/volume APIs did not locate a matching bound. No unverified Hadamard declaration is cited.

items.name: Elementary volume lower bound for the relation unit ball
items.statement: In an ell-dimensional Euclidean space with ell>=1, the closed unit ball has volume at least 2^ell*ell^(-ell/2), by containing the cube with each coordinate in [-1/sqrt(ell),1/sqrt(ell)].
items.note: Only the cube-in-ball consequence is new; Haar measure, finite products and orthonormal coordinates are existing infrastructure. For ell>=1 the coordinate cube of side 2/sqrt(ell) lies in the closed unit ball because its squared Euclidean norm is <=ell/ell. The paper's 'sphere' means ball. Measure is intrinsic to W, not the ambient M-dimensional measure.

items.name: Independent integral relations with product bound
items.statement: Minkowski second on L supplies ell independent integral relations E_1,...,E_ell, ordered by coefficient Euclidean norm, with product_i ||E_i||_2 <= ell^(ell/2)*D^(n/2). Each nonzero E_i has norm at least one.
items.note: Independent relations need not generate L as a Z-module. API: coefficient vectors, evaluation zero, independence and the product estimate.

items.name: Discarding the last n-1 relations
items.statement: For 1<=i<=ell, ||E_i||_2<=ell^[ell/(2*(ell+1-i))]*D^[n/(2*(ell+1-i))]. Therefore the first q=ell+1-n=M+1-2n relations all satisfy ||E_i||_2<=ell^(ell/(2n))*D^(1/2). Their complex span U has codimension n-1 in W_C.
items.note: Keep q exactly; removing n rather than n-1 loses the strict codimension needed for the next argument. Capacity implies q>=r, so selecting r retained relations is meaningful.

items.name: Full first jets give all gradients on the value kernel
items.statement: If V_C -> C^n direct_sum (C^r)^n is the surjective value-and-gradient map, then its gradient part restricts to a surjection W_C -> (C^r)^n, where W_C is the kernel of the value map.
items.locator: Section 3, p. 494, expanded input to the codimension argument
items.note: This is an elementary exact linear-algebra consequence of joint surjectivity, not the assertion that surjectivity of each separate projection would suffice.

items.name: A codimension-less-than-n subspace retains one full gradient block
items.statement: Let f:W->direct_sum_(a=1)^n k^r be surjective and U subset W have codimension < n. Then for some a, projection_a(f(U))=k^r. Applied with codim U=n-1, some retained-gradient matrix has rank r.
items.note: If all n block images are proper, their product has codimension >=n; f(U) lies in it, whereas surjectivity of f gives codim f(U)<=codim U<n. The joint codimension statement was not located as a library declaration; prove it from finite-dimensional rank inequalities. Separate surjectivity of each projection of f would not be sufficient.

items.name: One minor works at every conjugate
items.statement: Choose r retained relations with nonzero Jacobian determinant at one P_tau. For J=det(partial E_i/partial x_j), J(kappa) lies in K and is nonzero; every embedding of K into C is injective, so J(P_tau) is nonzero for every tau.
items.note: No Galois hypothesis on K/Q and no separate choice of relations for each embedding. The same equations must work at every conjugate.

items.name: Jacobian-open component model
items.statement: For r polynomials E in Q[x_1,...,x_r], define X_E=Spec((Q[x]/(E_1,...,E_r))[1/J]), J=det(partial E_i/partial x_j). This is the open part of the common zero scheme on which J is invertible.
items.note: API: localized quotient, projection to affine space, functor-of-points with E=0 and J invertible, base change, evaluation factorization. Tests r=1, E=x*(x-1) (two components), and E=x^2 (empty Jacobian-open over Q). Do not define the model as K itself or assert the whole relation ideal is generated by E.

items.name: Jacobian-open finite etale algebra and component extraction
items.statement: Over a characteristic-zero field, the Jacobian-open algebra for r equations in r variables is finite etale (possibly zero). If a finite separable extension K receives a surjective evaluation from this algebra, Spec K is an open-and-closed irreducible component.
items.locator: Section 1, pp. 487-488 and Proposition 2, p. 495, geometric inference
items.note: The baseline-standard-smooth and baseline-finite-etale items already supply the abstract Jacobian-presentation/etale and finite-product theorems. New here is assembling the r-equation localized quotient into that presentation and identifying the given surjective evaluation as a field factor/open-and-closed component. Preserve the zero-algebra case; a surjection to a field excludes it. This is an SF.0 comparison lemma, not a second theory of etale morphisms.

items.name: Proposition 2: explicit height bound for a component model
items.statement: For every K of degree n, d>=5 and r>=1 satisfying n(r+1)<=M=binom(d+r,d), put ell=M-n. There are r integral polynomials of total degree <=d with each coefficient of absolute value <= ell^(ell/(2n))*sqrt(M)*[n^2*d*(r+1)]^d*delta^(2d), whose Jacobian-open scheme contains Spec K as one irreducible component.
items.note: The selected kappa, relation list and invertible Jacobian are joint witnesses, not unrelated existential statements.

items.name: Logarithmic dimension and degree choice
items.statement: Let r be the least positive integer satisfying n(r+1)<=binom(2r,r), and set d=r. For all sufficiently large n one has r>=5, r<=3*log(n), and n(r+1)<=binom(2r,r)<=4*n*(r+1).
items.note: Use binom(2r,r)>=2^r and the Catalan quotient C_(r+1)/C_r=2(2r+1)/(r+2)<=4. Minimality at r-1 gives M<4n(r+1) when r>1; treat r=1 directly. The inequality r<=3 log(n) and r>=5 are eventual, not claims for n=1. Export an explicit sufficiently-large threshold when this is implemented.

items.name: Theorem 1: logarithmic-size number-field models
items.statement: There is an absolute constant Q>0 such that, for every number field K of degree n>=Q, some positive integers r,d<=Q*log(n) satisfy binom(d+r,r)<=Q*n*log(n), and r integral polynomials of total degree <=d and coefficients <=(n*delta)^(Q*log(n)) in absolute value give a Jacobian-open scheme containing Spec K as an irreducible component.
items.locator: Theorem 1, p. 487; proof in Section 4, pp. 495-496
items.note: Q is independent of the field and degree, and may be enlarged to absorb eventual thresholds. This is a description/height theorem, not a certified running-time bound.

items.name: Affine Bezout bound for isolated smooth zeros
items.statement: Over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, r polynomials in r variables of degrees <=d, with d>=1, have at most d^r common zeros where their Jacobian determinant is nonzero. This remains valid if their total common zero scheme has other, positive-dimensional components.
items.note: Couveignes cites Fulton Chapter 13. The publisher's Chapter 13 opening (p. 210, refined Bezout paragraph) explicitly bounds the sum of degrees of distinguished varieties and includes all irreducible components, without properness of the entire intersection. Homogenize the nonconstant equations at their actual degrees; each isolated affine point remains an isolated projective component. Zero or constant equations have empty Jacobian-open and are treated separately. No such multi-equation isolated bound was found in either pinned library. Full refined-intersection proof remains a supplier blueprint obligation; the statement and its applicability, not a fictional exact theorem number, are recorded.

items.name: Counting bounded coefficient lists
items.statement: For r ordered polynomials supported on the M degree-<=d monomials with integer coefficients of absolute value <=B, B>=0, there are exactly (2*floor(B)+1)^(r*M) such coefficient lists, including lower-degree and zero polynomials.
items.note: This is only the encoding of r coefficient vectors on the finite monomial set into a product of integer intervals; use existing finite-product and interval-cardinality APIs. The resulting cardinality is exact, including zero/lower-degree systems. B>=0 and floor(B) are essential. No new generic counting foundation is proposed.

items.name: Unweighted degree-n number-field count
items.statement: For n>=1 and real H>=1, N_n(H) is the cardinality of Q-algebra isomorphism classes of number fields of degree exactly n with |d_K|<=H. Count each class once; do not weight by automorphisms or count embeddings into a fixed ambient field.
items.note: ST.0 owns equivalence relations, height bounds and unweighted family counts. API: invariance, finiteness, monotonicity in H and the exact-degree condition. The existing fixed-ambient-field Hermite theorem is a different carrier that can supply finiteness after comparison.

items.name: Component cover gives a field-class bound
items.statement: If every class counted by N_n(H) has a Jacobian-open component model among S systems of r equations of degree <=d, then N_n(H)<=S*d^r. For each system, finite-etale field components give at most the number of its isolated geometric points, bounded by d^r; the map from admissible components to classes is surjective.
items.note: No injective assignment of fields to equation lists is required. The same field may have several models; this only increases the upper bound. Explicitly pass from geometric points to rational field components and then to isomorphism classes.

items.name: Theorem 2: degree-sensitive discriminant counting
items.statement: There is an absolute Q>0 such that for integers n>=Q and H>=1, N_n(H)<=n^(Q*n*(log(n))^3)*H^(Q*(log(n))^3).
items.note: Substitute delta<=H^(1/n) into the model-height bound, use r*M=O(n*(log n)^2), and absorb d^r and rounding by enlarging Q. The discriminant is absolute; the result is an upper bound, not an asymptotic N_n(H)~c_n H.

items.name: Product-measure covolume already in Mathlib
items.statement: For a number field K, with the standard product volume on its mixed embedding space, covol(O_K)=2^(-nrComplexPlaces K)*sqrt(|NumberField.discr K|).
items.locator: Section 2, pp. 489–490, normalization input; Mathlib Discriminant/Basic.lean, lines 89–133
items.note: This is NOT the paper's canonically weighted metric. The separate measure-normalization and discriminant-covolume items give the conversion.

items.name: Index is the quotient of full-lattice covolumes
items.statement: For full discrete Z-lattices L1<=L2 in R^iota (finite iota), covol(L1)/covol(L2)=[L2:L1]. Covolumes with a fixed Haar measure equal absolute basis determinants times the reference fundamental-domain measure.
items.locator: Section 3, p. 493, finite-index comparison; Mathlib ZLattice/Covolume.lean, lines 84–166
items.note: Use an orthonormal coordinate identification for a lattice in Wperp. The smaller lattice has larger covolume; no assertion that the transpose image is all of Lperp.

items.name: Existing degree-bounded polynomial module and monomial basis
items.statement: Over a commutative ring R, restrictTotalDegree sigma R d is the submodule of MvPolynomial sigma R consisting exactly of total-degree-<=d polynomials. Its support restriction has the basis indexed by monomials of total degree <=d; for finite sigma this module is finite.
items.note: Use basisRestrictSupport on the total-degree exponent set and the anonymous Module.Finite instance. The binomial count and homogeneous-section comparison are the separate bounded-polynomials item.

items.name: Existing Schwartz–Zippel input to bounded parameters
items.statement: For a nonzero polynomial p in N variables over an integral domain and a finite set S, the fraction of zeros on S^N is <=p.totalDegree/#S. In characteristic zero, totalDegree(p)<=D and S={0,...,D} imply that some grid value is nonzero.
items.locator: Section 3, p. 492, bounded-grid application; Mathlib Algebra/MvPolynomial/SchwartzZippel.lean, lines 188–206
items.note: The strict fraction D/(D+1)<1 gives the displayed existence by elementary finite counting. This supplies the actual determinant application after its total-degree bound. It does not assert the stronger per-variable-degree theorem.

items.name: Existing submersive-presentation route to etaleness
items.statement: A finite submersive presentation P of an R-algebra S with relative dimension zero supplies IsStandardSmoothOfRelativeDimension 0 R S; such an algebra is etale over R.
items.locator: Section 3, p. 495, Jacobian criterion; Mathlib Smooth/StandardSmooth.lean, lines 87–103; StandardSmoothCotangent.lean, lines 348–355
items.note: The concluding Etale instance is anonymous and is not assigned an invented theorem name. Constructing the concrete presentation of the localized r-equation quotient remains jacobian-etale-components.

items.name: Etale algebras over a field are finite products of separable extensions
items.statement: For a field k and a commutative k-algebra A, Etale k A holds iff A is k-algebra-isomorphic to a finite product of finite separable field extensions of k; the index set can be empty.
items.locator: Section 1, pp. 487–488 and Section 3, p. 495; Mathlib Etale/Field.lean, lines 267–286
items.note: This already gives finiteness, not merely formal etaleness. Do not prove a second etale-algebra classification or discard the zero ring/empty product.

items.name: Hadamard bound for a complex Gram determinant
items.statement: For vectors v_1,...,v_n in a finite-dimensional complex inner-product space, their Hermitian Gram determinant is nonnegative and at most product_i ||v_i||_2^2. In particular, if each squared norm is <=D with D>=0, det Gram(v)<=D^n.
items.note: Use Gram–Schmidt (or a positive-semidefinite matrix factorization), determinant multiplication and norm-decrease of orthogonal projection; retain the linearly dependent case, where the determinant is zero. This generic inequality is separated from the arithmetic relation-covolume estimate. Matching Gram positivity and Gram–Schmidt APIs exist, but no exact determinant upper bound was located; the entrywise Hadamard product is unrelated.

prerequisites.why: The generic first-jet theorem has no current owner; GenericDoublePointInterpolation is proposed. BO Sections 1–6 (pp. 1–19) read completely, including induction and exceptions. routes.title: Generic double-point interpolation in characteristic zero
routes.reason: The catalogue-wide screen found no owner of generic double-point interpolation or the Alexander–Hirschowitz theorem. R09.1/2 own projective/Hilbert/Quot foundations, not the Hilbert function of generic fat-point configurations; SF.0 owns schemes, not this interpolation theorem. The separate interpolation project has a reusable endpoint independent of number-field enumeration.
routes.brief: Prove the characteristic-zero, exception-free Alexander–Hirschowitz interface used by Couveignes: for an algebraically closed field k, r>=1, d>=5, n>=1 and n(r+1)<=binom(d+r,d), a nonempty Zariski-open set of ordered distinct n-tuples in (A^r_k)^n has surjective value-and-first-derivative evaluation on degree-<=d polynomials. Import SchemeAndStackFoundations (Scheme, stack, cohomology and intersection foundations), especially SF.0, and AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry (Algebraic moduli and representability for arithmetic geometry), R09.1/R09.2 only for the projective parameter/Hilbert-family interfaces actually used. Reuse Mathlib MvPolynomial.restrictTotalDegree and its restricted monomial basis; construct the binomial dimension, fixed-degree homogenization/H^0 comparison, length-n(r+1) double-point quotient and first-jet matrix. Follow Brambilla–Ottaviani Sections 2–6: residual/trace sequences, restriction-dimension inequalities, curvilinear reduction, semicontinuity and differential-Horace degeneration, cubic cases and quartic base cases with exact rank certificates where the source invokes computer calculations. The induction needs low-degree inputs even though the exported theorem assumes d>=5. Supply the affine-chart/open-minor comparison and integer-parameter specialization, using the existing total-degree Schwartz–Zippel theorem whenever possible; the stronger per-variable box lemma is a small API consequence, not a new polynomial foundation. EffectiveBoundsCompactModels consumes this result. Tests must reject special collinear configurations, recover univariate Hermite interpolation, and separate double points from reduced points and higher jets. Do not export positive-characteristic or low-degree exception-free claims.

routes.title: Effective arithmetic bounds and geometry of numbers, Part II: compact models and degree-sensitive field counts
routes.reason: The fully read tauceti:Completed/EffectiveBounds anchor already constructs effective Hermite–Minkowski bounds; its pinned implementation counts bounded-discriminant subfields of a fixed ambient extension by primitive-element polynomial bounds. Couveignes adds short multi-equation component models and the sharper degree-sensitive discriminant exponent, neither of which the anchor promises. This is an extension with the anchor as first prerequisite. ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0 supplies the isomorphism-class count carrier, and ST.3 is a consumer; its selected asymptotic/moment goals do not duplicate the model construction.
routes.brief: Extend tauceti:Completed/EffectiveBounds (Effective arithmetic bounds and geometry of numbers) as the FIRST prerequisite; import its completed explicit Hermite–Minkowski and discriminant infrastructure without reconstructing it. Fix n=[K:Q], delta=|disc K|^(1/n), and the weighted canonical measure. For d>=5, r>=1, M=binom(d+r,d)>=n(r+1), ell=M-n, prove Proposition 2 exactly: r integral polynomials of total degree <=d, coefficient height <=ell^(ell/(2n))*sqrt(M)*[n^2*d*(r+1)]^d*delta^(2d), whose Jacobian-open scheme contains Spec K as an irreducible component. Build the short independent integers (all conjugates <=delta^2), integral parameter choice, saturated relation lattice, finite-index transpose image and Gram estimate, retain exactly ell+1-n short relations, choose one gradient block of full rank, and transport the SAME nonzero Jacobian minor through every embedding. Import GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic (Geometry of numbers, quadratic forms and homogeneous arithmetic), GN.0/GN.1 for covolume consequences and the genuine second-minimum witness theorem; GenericDoublePointInterpolation (Generic double-point interpolation in characteristic zero) for the first-jet theorem; SchemeAndStackFoundations (Scheme, stack, cohomology and intersection foundations), SF.0/SF.5 for the localized component comparison and isolated-point Bezout. Use ArithmeticStatistics (Arithmetic statistics, counting fields and Selmer distributions), ST.0 for unweighted exact-degree Q-isomorphism classes, supplying a bridge from fixed-ambient finiteness, without making the construction depend on ST.3's statistical asymptotics. Deduce Theorem 1: one absolute Q, n>=Q, r,d<=Q log n, M<=Q n log n, coefficient height <=(n*delta)^(Q log n). Then prove Theorem 2: for integers n>=Q and H>=1, N_n(H)<=n^(Q*n*(log n)^3)*H^(Q*(log n)^3). Give the coefficient-box count, bound isolated components by d^r despite other positive-dimensional components, and use a surjection from component models to classes, not an injective choice of models. Preserve all measure factors, floor functions and eventual thresholds. Test a non-integral-basis short family, a strict dual-image index, repeated roots, multiple field components and n=1 outside the eventual range. Neither algorithmic runtime, an asymptotic equivalent c_n*H, nor an integral presentation of O_K is claimed.
